items.h: Stefon Diggs Expected to Return to Practice on Thursday
items.s: According to Tashan Reed of The Washington Post, Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that wide receiver Stefon Diggs (hand, hamstring) wasn't going to practice on Wednesday, but that the veteran will be a full participant for Thursday's session. Diggs officially logged a "DNP" for Wednesday's practice with an injury note of hand/hamstring/NIR (Rest). This appears to simply be a rest day for the 32-year-old Diggs, and there doesn't seem to be any reason for concern. With fellow wide receiver Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn patellar tendon in his left knee, Diggs has an opportunity to play a large role for the Commanders. Diggs has recorded…

items.h: DNP due to 'hand/hamstring/rest'
items.s: Diggs (hand/hamstring/rest) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice. Head coach Dan Quinn relayed to Tashan Reed of The Washington Post earlier Wednesday that Diggs wasn't going to practice for an unspecified reason. The Commanders ended up listing hand and hamstring issues in addition to rest, the latter of which is the likeliest reason for his absence because Diggs is expected to be a full participant Thursday. With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the season, Diggs will be on the receiving end of plenty of targets from QB Jayden Daniels as long as Diggs is able to suit up on game days.

items.h: Stefon Diggs (undisclosed) to return to practice Thursday
items.s: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Stefon Diggs will return to practice on Thursday. Diggs is not practicing on Wednesday due to an undisclosed reason. He will be a full participant on Thursday.

items.h: Sitting out, but will be full go Thursday
items.s: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that Diggs won't practice Wednesday for to an unspecified reason but is expected to be a full participant Thursday, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports. Though Diggs isn't on the practice field coming off of a Week 7 bye, Quinn noted that the wideout's absence isn't related to his prior hand injury nor any other health concern, per Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic. Instead, Diggs appears to be getting more of a veteran's rest day, which Quinn added will likely be the norm for the receiver to begin practice weeks moving forward. With Terry McLaurin sustaining a season-ending knee injury in a Week 6 loss to the 49ers, Diggs should be locked in as…

With Terry McLaurin sustaining a season-ending knee injury in a Week 6 loss to the 49ers, Diggs should be locked in as Washington's No. 1 wideout for the rest of the season, though players such as Antonio Williams,…

items.h: Stefon Diggs won't see bigger role due to Terry McLaurin injury
items.s: Stefon Diggs reportedly won't see a larger role due to the injury to Terry McLaurin, per HC Dan Quinn. The absence of the star receiver will be made up for by others, with Antonio Williams being one of those named. This could easily be coach speak as the Commanders certainly need Diggs' help with McLaurin out. However, the naming of Antonio Williams was a pleasant surprise, as the rookie has flashed when given the opportunity to perform. He's a fun name to watch as the season moves on.

items.h: Stefon Diggs Won't See a Workload Change with Teammate's Injury
items.s: Washington Commanders veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs (hamstring) missed the team's Week 5 tie with the Giants and again appeared on the injury report with a hamstring concern ahead of a Week 6 loss to the 49ers. Coming out of a Week 7 bye, head coach Dan Quinn told reporters on Monday that the 32-year-old is doing "well", but he is not anticipating a drastic workload change following the season-ending injury to Terry McLaurin (knee). Diggs has seen a 59.8% snap share through his five games played, and Quinn appears content to keep him in that range, telling the media that others in the wide receiver room will be tasked with more responsibility, specifically highlighting rookie Antonio…

items.h: Stefon Diggs scores TD in Week 6
items.s: Stefon Diggs caught six of his seven targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in a 23-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 6's Monday night game. Diggs set a season-high in catches for the Commanders in the close loss to San Francisco. He found the end zone for the fourth time this season on a one-yard pass from Jayden Daniels late in the third quarter. Diggs should remain a key piece of the Washington passing attack, especially after Terry McLaurin had to be carted off the field with a knee injury on Monday night. The Commanders are on bye in Week 7 before they take on the Eagles in Week 8. Diggs can be considered a solid flex option in fantasy going forward.

items.h: Scores TD in return from injury
items.s: Diggs brought in six of seven targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night. Diggs made a splash in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury, recording a one-yard touchdown grab late in the third quarter to begin a Commanders comeback from a 23-3 deficit. The veteran wideout finished with the second-highest reception total of the night for Washington while also setting the pace in targets, and his catch tally also was a new season high, which likely was aided by an early exit from fellow WR Terry McLaurin due to an apparent serious knee injury. Diggs will take a 24-214-4 line into a Week 7 bye before returning to action…

items.h: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) active for Week 6
items.s: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is officially active for Week 6 for the Washington Commanders according to Adam Schefter.

items.h: Back in action Monday
items.s: Diggs (hamstring) is listed as active Monday at San Francisco. Diggs is back in action after missing Week 5 due to a hamstring injury. He'll be among QB Jayden Daniels' key receivers Monday against a 49ers defense that ranks seventh in the NFL versus the pass (199.6 yards per game) this season as he looks to build upon an 18-170-3 line on 31 targets in four appearances as a Commander.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) is listed as active Monday at San Francisco.
items.s: Diggs is back in action after missing Week 5 due to a hamstring injury. He'll be among QB Jayden Daniels' key receivers Monday against a 49ers defense that ranks seventh in the NFL versus the pass (199.6 yards per game) this season as he looks to build upon an 18-170-3 line on 31 targets in four appearances as a Commander.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring), who is listed as questionable for Monday's game at San Francisco, is in line to play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: Diggs sat out the Commanders' Week 5 tie with the Giants due to a hamstring issue and then was able to manage a pair of limited practices during Week 6 prep, eventually getting tagged as questionable ahead of Monday's contest. Assuming he avoids the Commanders' inactive list, as expected, Diggs will join Terry McLaurin as the top wide receivers available to quarterback Jayden Daniels.

items.h: Fantasy football Week 6 inactives: Jeremiyah Love, DJ Moore out
items.s: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against San Francisco.
items.s: Diggs ended the week with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. Diggs did not play in Week 5 against the Giants, but if he's cleared to play against the 49ers, then it would be the first time that he, Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels are on the field together since Week 2 against the Cowboys. If Diggs does not play, then Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks would both operate in elevated roles offensively behind McLaurin.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) was on the field for Saturday's practice session, Jonah Keim of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Diggs is on the practice field for a second consecutive day. He was unable to play against the Giants in Week 5 due to a hamstring injury, and his official status for Monday night's game against the 49ers will be more clear once the Commanders announce their injury designations after Saturday's practice.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) was limited at Friday's practice.
items.s: This marks Diggs' first notable on-field work since Week 4 prep as he deals with a hamstring injury, which held him out of a Week 5 tie with the Giants. Both Diggs and No. 1 WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring), who was given a veteran's rest day Friday, are tending to health concerns at the moment, and Saturday's practice likely will be key to determine if either of them get designations for Monday's game in San Francisco.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) was going through stretching at Friday's practice, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: After sitting out Thursday's practice, Diggs is showing at least modest signs of progress ahead of a Monday matchup with the 49ers. He missed last week's game against the Giants, while Terry McLaurin returned from a hamstring injury of his own.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) won't practice Thursday, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.
items.s: Diggs sat out Washington's Week 5 tie against the Giants, and he won't participate in the Commanders' first practice ahead of Monday's Week 6 matchup against the 49ers. The veteran wide receiver gets the benefit of an extra day to recover from his hamstring injury, but his fantasy managers could face a difficult decision with few replacements available if Diggs' availability isn't clarified one way or another by the time Washington releases game statuses Saturday.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) won't play Sunday against the Giants, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports after Commanders coach Dan Quinn provided injury updates Friday.
items.s: After missing practice time earlier in the week, Diggs has now been ruled out for Week 5. Terry McLaurin, on the other hand, is expected to play through a hamstring injury, though Quinn wasn't quite ready to guarantee it Friday afternoon. With Diggs definitely out, there will be extra WR snaps available for some combination of Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
items.s: With Diggs having already missed practice Wednesday and Thursday, his continued absence leaves his status for Sunday's game against the Giants in question. Teammate Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is also uncertain, though he's reportedly present for the start of practice Friday.

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) didn't participate in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Though he didn't mix into drills, Diggs was present for the open portion of Thursday's practice and was seen working out off to the side under the supervision of trainers, per Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic. Washington also listed fellow receiver Terry McLaurin (hamstring) as a non-participant, giving him and Diggs just one more chance apiece to practice this week before the Commanders potentially make rulings on both players ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants. Currently, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Luke McCaffrey are the healthy options at the position on…

items.h: Diggs (hamstring) was present for the start of practice Thursday, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.
items.s: Diggs and fellow wideout Terry McLaurin (hamstring) both sat out practice Wednesday. While McLaurin wasn't spotted Thursday after missing this past Sunday's loss to the Colts in London, Diggs looks poised to take a step forward in terms of activity. Thursday's injury report will reveal the extent of Diggs' participation.

items.h: Diggs was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury.
items.s: Diggs wasn't spotted on the field during the portion of Wednesday's session open to the media, and now the reason for his absence is known. Both he and fellow WR Terry McLaurin weren't able to mix into drills to begin Week 5 prep due to hamstring issues, leaving massive question marks for the state of the Commanders' passing game ahead of Sunday's contest against the Giants. Practice reports Thursday and Friday ultimately will be telling for the statuses of McLaurin and Diggs.

items.h: Diggs (undisclosed) was not on the practice field during the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Losing Diggs to an injury is the last thing the Commanders need after Terry McLaurin went down in practice with a hamstring injury last week, causing him to miss last Sunday's loss to the Colts. Washington leaned on rookie Antonio Williams and veterans Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks behind Diggs against Indy.

items.h: Diggs caught five of nine targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
items.s: While the targets and receptions led the Commanders on the day, Diggs finished just fourth in receiving yards on the team as his longest gain went for only 10 yards. The veteran wideout's ability to deliver a big play was impacted by the loss of Marcus Mariota (knee) in the first quarter, leaving the offense in the hands of seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis. Diggs could be the No. 1 receiver again in Week 5 against the Giants if Terry McLaurin (hamstring) remains sidelined, but Diggs' ceiling could be limited if Jayden Daniels (elbow) isn't cleared to return.

items.h: Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports that Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is expected to miss Sunday's game against the Colts in London, which would leave Diggs as the top wide receiver for the Commanders.
items.s: McLaurin drew the questionable tag for Week 4 after sustaining a hamstring injury during Friday's practice. His status for Sunday's International game has yet to be confirmed, but in the event that McLaurin is indeed ruled out, Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams would be in line for larger roles against Indianapolis. Diggs has caught four passes or more in each of the first three games of the regular season and has a 13-135-3 receiving line on 22 targets.

items.h: Diggs caught four of seven targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seahawks.
items.s: Diggs finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Terry McLaurin, but he was unable to make it three straight games with a touchdown. Diggs has now recorded at least four receptions in each of his first three contests as a member of the Commanders, reeling in 13 of 22 targets for 135 yards and three scores. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota proved to be a viable starter in Week 3 with Jayden Daniels (elbow) unavailable, so fantasy managers don't have to worry about Diggs moving forward.

items.h: Diggs caught five of six targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders' 37-20 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.s: Diggs tied Rachaad White and Dyami Brown for second on the team with his six targets, three behind Terry McLaurin for the team lead. It was Diggs who accounted for both of Washington's touchdowns, securing scores from Jayden Daniels (elbow) in the second quarter before then catching one from Marcus Mariota in the fourth. Through two games with the Commanders, Diggs has nine catches for 102 yards and three touchdowns on 15 targets. His production figures to take a hit while Daniels is sidelined with his injury.

items.h: Diggs brought in four of nine targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in a Week 1 loss to the Eagles on Sunday.
items.s: Diggs' nine targets were more than double the amount of any other Washington player. While the veteran wideout wasn't very efficient with those targets, he finished second on the team in receiving yards and put up a strong fantasy score thanks to a 10-yard TD connection with Jayden Daniels in the fourth quarter. Fantasy managers who roster Diggs should be encouraged by the amount of attention he got from Daniels in the pair's first regular-season action together, while presumed top WR Terry McLaurin totaled just two catches on four targets. McLaurin figures to be more involved most weeks,…

items.h: Diggs is among the seven wide receivers on Washington's initial 53-man roster.
items.s: The depth chart behind Diggs appears uncertain, but the veteran wide receiver seems safely locked into a starting role opposite Terry McLaurin heading into the regular season. Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown, Treylon Burks, Jaylin Lane and Luke McCaffrey also made the team. Diggs has fallen short of 1,000 receiving yards only once in the past eight regular seasons.

items.h: Diggs is expected to make his preseason debut Saturday against Detroit, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Diggs, Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels are all lined up to play Saturday after all three sat out of the Commanders' preseason opener against the Dolphins on Friday, Aug. 14. Diggs joined the Commanders in early August on a one-year, $12 million contract after playing for the Patriots in 2025. He's slated to serve as the team's WR2 behind McLaurin, with Luke McCaffrey, Treylon Burks and rookie third-rounder Antonio Williams all competing for the No. 3 role.

items.h: Diggs isn't in line to play in Friday's preseason contest versus the Dolphins.
items.s: After the Patriots released Diggs in March, he finally found in a landing spot in the early stages of training camp, inking a one-year, $12 million contract to join the Commanders. While he has a week of practice under his belt with his new squad, he'll have to wait until at least Saturday, Aug. 22 at Detroit to get some in-game preseason reps with new QB Jayden Daniels and top WR Terry McLaurin. In 17 regular-season games for New England last season, Diggs put together an 85-1,013-4 line on 102 targets.

items.h: Diggs is slated to sign a one-year, $12 million contract with the Commanders, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Diggs helped pace the Patriots' fourth-ranked pass offense in 2025, reeling in 85 of 102 targets for 1,013 yards and four touchdowns in 17 regular-season contests. New England released him at the start of the new league year in March, and after legal issues were settled in May and the NFL closed its review of potential violations of the personal conduct policy in June, wide receiver-needy teams like the Commanders have been tied to him. With Washington finally coming to terms with Diggs, he'll join Terry McLaurin at the top of the WR corps for QB Jayden Daniels.

items.h: The Commanders and Diggs agreed to a contract Wednesday, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
items.s: Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, the two sides have been circling the wagons, and now Diggs will join his fourth different team in as many seasons. Diggs is coming off an 85-1,013-4 line on 102 targets in 17 regular-season games with the Patriots last season en route to an appearance in Super Bowl LX. In Washington, he'll create a top WR pairing with Terry McLaurin and be on the receiving end of passes from third-year QB Jayden Daniels.

items.h: Diggs is reportedly on the Commanders' radar, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com.
items.s: Per Fowler, the Commanders are in wait-and-see mode in terms of their wide receiver corps, but the team is monitoring the situation with Diggs, who the report suggests is intrigued by the chance to play for Washington. For now, Terry McLaurin is the team's clear-cut top WR, with all of Antonio Williams, Luke McCaffrey, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane and Van Jefferson competing for slotting behind McLaurin.

items.h: According to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, "at least five teams have been checking in on Diggs" ahead of the opening of NFL training camps.
items.s: After putting up a 85-1,013-4 line on 102 targets in 17 regular-season games during his only campaign with the Patriots, Diggs was let go in March and has yet to catch on elsewhere. While Fowler's report doesn't suggest that anything is imminent, Diggs does eventually figure to catch on with a team looking to bolster its WR depth, and depending on his landing spot, the 32-year-old could yield decent fantasy utility relative to his current average draft position.

items.h: Diggs said on his YouTube channel that "You can't name a No. 2 better than me" when referring to wide receivers across the NFL, ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Diggs still views himself as one of the NFL's best wide receivers and believes he could earn a starting role on any team. The 32-year-old free agent exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in the 2025 regular season as the top option in the passing game for the Patriots, which marked the seventh time in the last eight campaigns that Diggs topped 1,000 yards. New England opted to cut Diggs rather than pay his $26.5 million salary cap hit in 2026, but he presumably wants to be paid like a starting wideout wherever he plays next.

items.h: Diggs recently told FOX 5 Washington DC that he anticipates signing with a team soon and has interest in playing for the Commanders.
items.s: Diggs grew up in Gaithersburg, Md., played his college ball at the University of Maryland and still lives in the same area during the NFL offseason. The Commanders, meanwhile, have more than $40 million in cap space and lack experienced starters at wide receiver opposite Terry McLaurin. It's not hard to connect the dots, especially after Diggs told a Washington news program that a homecoming was one of the first things he thought about when the Patriots released him in March. The NFL recently closed its review of Diggs for an alleged December dispute with his private chef, and now that a…

items.h: The NFL has closed its review of Diggs after determining that there was insufficient evidence of a personal conduct policy violation stemming from an alleged dispute with his private chef this past December, ESPN.com…
items.s: Friday's decision arrives after Diggs was found not guilty last month of assaulting his private chef in a pay dispute, but at the time of the verdict NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy noted that the matter remained "under review of the personal conduct policy." Diggs, who was released by the Patriots in March, has yet to catch on elsewhere, but on the heels of a 2025 regular season in which he recorded an 85-1,013-4 line on 102 targets in 17 games, the 32-year-old is a candidate to garner interest in the coming weeks from teams still seeking to bolster their WR corps.
